function.name: run_streaming_simulation
function.description: Runs an interactive physical simulation on HTML5 Canvas. The simulation runs in real-time on a retro oscilloscope/radar player. The Pascal program must output coordinates as JSON lines (e.g. WriteLn('{"x": 1.0, "y": 2.0}')) with a short delay (e.g. using Sleep(50) from SysUtils) to create smooth streaming curves.

title.description: The title of the physical simulation (e.g. 'Damped Pendulum', 'Lissajous Curves', 'Chaotic Attractor')

type.description: The visual display style of the Canvas Player. Use 'oscilloscope' for standard waves/particles, 'radar' for scanning/sonar sweeps, and 'graph' for progressive y(x) plots.

code.description: A self-contained Pascal program. Must print coordinates to standard output at regular intervals (using Sleep(30) or Sleep(50) from SysUtils) in JSON format. You MUST include the appropriate standard Pascal libraries in your `uses` clause (e.g. Math, SysUtils, Classes, StrUtils) depending on the functions you use. If you encounter a Compilation Error, analyze it. If you lack the knowledge to fix it, use `search_knowledge_base` or `search_web` to find the correct standard library for the missing identifier, then retry execution. If you successfully resolve an error, you MUST call `save_to_knowledge_base` to store the solution for future reference. Example: program Wave; uses Math, SysUtils; var t: Double; begin for t := 0 to 100 do begin WriteLn('{"x": ' + FloatToStr(t/10) + ', "y": ' + FloatToStr(sin(t/10)) + '}'); end; end.
